title: Witch's Wardrobe: Elements
premise: A witch-themed timed outfit-matching game where the player cycles magical wardrobe parts to recreate a target look before time runs out.
interaction_model: Single-screen tap/click play with left-right cycling controls for three outfit slots and a manual submit button to validate the combination.
objective: Match the target head, body, and hand item combination exactly, then submit it to earn score and extra time.
progression: Arcade score-chasing progression with repeated random target combinations, time pressure, score accumulation, success time bonuses, failure time penalties, and restart-on-game-over replayability.
theme: Whimsical magical fashion, witchcraft, moonlit fantasy dressing room, and light spooky enchantment.
mood: Playful, cozy, colorful, arcadey, and slightly Halloween-like.
likely_audience: Casual players, kids, mobile-first browser players, and anyone who enjoys dress-up, matching, or quick fantasy mini-games.
confidence_notes: High confidence in the main mechanic because all gameplay logic is visible in a single HTML file.
High confidence that the game is a timed outfit matcher rather than a traditional open-ended dress-up sandbox.
Moderate confidence in genre labeling because the presentation resembles dress-up while the actual loop behaves like a score-attack matching puzzle.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen browser mini-game called "Witch's Wardrobe: Elements" where the player must dress a cartoon witch to match a randomly generated target outfit before a countdown expires. Show a top HUD with three target icons for head, body, and hand equipment, plus score and remaining time. In the center, render a full witch character on an animated moonlit fantasy stage with stars, glow effects, and magical ambience. At the bottom, provide large left/right arrow controls for Head, Body, and Hand so the player can cycle through exactly five options in each slot. Include themed variants such as pointy hat, flower crown, hood, horns, or moon tiara for headwear; robe, nature dress, royal gown, bone motif, or starry dress for bodywear; and broom, wand, lantern, potion, or spellbook for the hand item. The player presses a big "Cast Spell" button to submit the current combination. If all three slots match the target exactly, award a sizable score bonus plus extra time, flash success feedback, play a positive sound, show celebratory magical effects, and generate a new target. If the combination is wrong, subtract time, show a fail reaction, and keep the same target so the player can try again. Use a 60-second starting timer, fast replayable arcade pacing, bright fantasy UI panels, dramatic title and result screens, and touch-friendly controls that feel good on mobile as well as desktop.
